dataset_metadata.disclaimer: New AI-generated English drafts of the recorded Classical Chinese; not scholarly reviewed. Original source interpretations are not verified geometry or modern etymology.

shuowen:1001.text: A manner of running. Formed from 走, with 㕡 indicating the sound. Read like 紃.

shuowen:1002.text: The sense of running. Formed from 走, with 薊 indicating the sound. Read like 結 in 髽結, tying up the hair.

shuowen:1003.text: The sense of running. Formed from 走, with 囷 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1004.text: The sense of running. Formed from 走, with 坐 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1005.text: The sense of running. Formed from 走, with 憲 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1006.text: The sense of running. Formed from 走, with 臱 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1007.text: To run. Formed from 走, with 𢧜 indicating the sound. Read like 秩秩 in the Odes' “Dignified and orderly in bearing.”

shuowen:1008.text: To run. Formed from 走, with 有 indicating the sound. Read like 又.

shuowen:1009.text: To run lightly. Formed from 走, with 烏 indicating the sound. Read like 鄔.

shuowen:1010.text: The appearance of running while looking back. Formed from 走, with 瞿 indicating the sound. Read like 劬.

shuowen:1011.text: A manner of running. Formed from 走, with abbreviated 蹇 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1012.text: Doubting and hesitating before departing. Formed from 走, with 才 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1013.text: To ford shallow water. Formed from 走, with 此 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1014.text: To walk alone. Formed from 走, with 勻 indicating the sound. Read like 煢.

shuowen:1015.text: To walk calmly. Formed from 走, with 與 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1016.text: To be able to stand. Formed from 走, with 巳 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1017.text: The sense of lingering. Formed from 走, with 里 indicating the sound. Read like 孩, a small child.

shuowen:1018.text: To walk. Formed from 走, with 臭 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1019.text: To walk rapidly with lowered head. Formed from 走, with 金 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1020.text: 趌𧼨: to run in anger. Formed from 走, with 吉 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1021.text: The manner 趌𧼨. Formed from 走, with 曷 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1022.text: Swift. Formed from 走, with 瞏 indicating the sound. Read like 讙.

shuowen:1023.text: To walk straight ahead. Formed from 走, with 气 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1024.text: The manner of hastening forward, 𧾰如. Formed from 走, with 翼 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1025.text: To kick. Formed from 走, with abbreviated 決 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1026.text: The sound of walking. Another explanation: the appearance of not walking. Formed from 走, with 異 indicating the sound. Read like 敕.

shuowen:1027.text: To hasten. Formed from 走, with 氐 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1028.text: In the expression 趨趙: to walk slowly or linger. Formed from 走, with 多 indicating the sound. [The transmitted gloss 久 is disputed; commentary favors 夂, “a slow gait.”]

shuowen:1029.text: To walk slowly or linger, as in the old expression 趨趙. Formed from 走, with 肖 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1030.text: To walk with difficulty. Formed from 走, with 斤 indicating the sound. Read like 堇.

shuowen:1031.text: The sense of running. Formed from 走, with 夐 indicating the sound. Read like 繘.

shuowen:1032.text: Far. Formed from 走, with 卓 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1033.text: A far-reaching manner of movement, 趠䟑. Formed from 走, with 龠 indicating the sound. [The precise gait is uncertain.]

shuowen:1034.text: To take large steps. Formed from 走, with 矍 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1035.text: To leap exceptionally far or high. Formed from 走, with 契 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1036.text: To run. Formed from 走, with 幾 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1037.text: To run. Formed from 走, with 岪 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1038.text: To run wildly. Formed from 走, with 矞 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1039.text: To walk slowly. Formed from 走, with 曼 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1040.text: To run. Formed from 走, with 出 indicating the sound. Read like 屈 meaning without a tail.

shuowen:1041.text: To be at an impasse. Formed from 走, with 匊 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1042.text: 趑趄: walking without advancing. Formed from 走, with 次 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1043.text: The hesitant manner 趑趄. Formed from 走, with 且 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1044.text: A limping gait, 𧽐𧽐. Formed from 走, with 虔 indicating the sound. Read like 愆.

shuowen:1045.text: Walking in the manner 䟒趢. Another explanation: walking with a bent back. Formed from 走, with 雚 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1046.text: The manner 䟒趢. Formed from 走, with 录 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1047.text: To move or run rapidly, especially in the reduplicated expression 䞭䞭. Formed from 走, with 夋 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1048.text: To walk sideways. Formed from 走, with 朿 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Though the earth is said to be thick, I dare not fail to step cautiously.”

shuowen:1049.text: Half a pace. Formed from 走, with 圭 indicating the sound. Pronounced the same as 跬.

shuowen:1050.text: 䞾騭: frivolous or flighty. Formed from 走, with 虒 indicating the sound. Read like 池.

shuowen:1051.text: To fall prostrate. Formed from 走, with 咅 indicating the sound. Read like 匐.

shuowen:1052.text: To brace or tread forcefully, particularly in the Han military expression for drawing a strong crossbow with the feet. Formed from 走, with an abbreviated 㡿 indicating the sound. A Han ordinance mentions a hundred crossbow-drawers. [Duan discusses conflicting readings 䞣張 and 蹶張 and competing glyph analyses.]

shuowen:1053.text: To move. Formed from 走, with 樂 indicating the sound. Read like 䟏 in the Spring and Autumn commentary's “Fu Luo.”

shuowen:1054.text: To move. Formed from 走, with 隹 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn commentary says: “They covenanted at Cui.” Cui is a place name.

shuowen:1055.text: To rotate or exchange cultivated plots and the associated place of residence under an ancient system of reallocating farmland. Formed from 走, with 亘 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1056.text: To stumble while running. Formed from 走, with 眞 indicating the sound. Read like 顚.

shuowen:1057.text: To stamp or leap in a mourning rite, often in the expression 擗踊. Formed from 走, with 甬 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1058.text: To halt movement. Another explanation: the name of a sacrifice at the stove. Formed from 走, with 畢 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1059.text: To advance. Formed from 走, with 斬 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1060.text: 趧𡝤: dances of the peoples of the four quarters, each having its own tunes. Formed from 走, with 是 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1061.text: The gait of a sparrow. Formed from 走, with 兆 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1062.text: To run with tail raised. Formed from 走, with 干 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1063.text: The base below. It depicts plants emerging with a footing, hence 止 is used for a foot. All characters in the 止 category are formed from 止.

shuowen:1064.text: The heel. Formed from 止, with 重 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1065.text: To brace, prop up, or resist. Formed from 止, with 尚 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1066.text: To hesitate, 䠧. Formed from 止, with 寺 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1067.text: To stop. Formed from 止, with 巨 indicating the sound. Another explanation: to thrust; another: to leap across, 超歫.

shuowen:1068.text: To advance without walking is called 歬. Formed from 止 above 舟.

shuowen:1069.text: To pass through. Formed from 止, with 厤 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1070.text: To arrive. Formed from 止, with 叔 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1071.text: A person unable to walk. Formed from 止, with 辟 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1072.text: A woman marrying. Formed from 止 and abbreviated 婦, with 𠂤 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1073.text: Swift. Formed from 止 and 又; 又 is a hand. 屮 indicates the sound.

shuowen:1074.text: That beneath a loom which the foot treads upon. Formed from 止 and 又, with 入 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1075.text: To tread. Formed from reversed 止. Read like 撻.

shuowen:1076.text: Not smooth. Formed from four 止.

shuowen:1077.text: Feet spread apart. Formed from 止 and 𣥂. All characters in the 癶 category are formed from 癶. Read like 撥.

shuowen:1078.text: To mount a carriage. Formed from 癶 and 豆, depicting mounting a carriage.

shuowen:1079.text: To trample plants flat with the feet. Formed from 癶 and 殳. The Spring and Autumn commentary says: “Trample them flat, heap them up and pile them high.”

shuowen:1080.text: To walk. Formed from 止 and 𣥂 facing away from each other. All characters in the 步 category are formed from 步.

shuowen:1081.text: Jupiter. It traverses the twenty-eight lunar lodges, spreading through yin and yang, moving one station in twelve months. Formed from 步, with 戌 indicating the sound. The Treatise on Pitch-Pipes and the Calendar calls the five planets the five steps.

shuowen:1082.text: To stop. Formed from 止 and 匕; 匕 means to stand next in sequence. All characters in the 此 category are formed from 此.

shuowen:1083.text: Weak or defective. The explanation is missing.

shuowen:1084.text: To recognize. Formed from 此, with 朿 indicating the sound. Another explanation: to conceal.

shuowen:1085.text: A speech particle appearing in the Songs of Chu. Formed from 此 and 二. Its meaning is not fully known.

shuowen:1086.text: Correct. Formed from 止, with 一 marking the stopping point. All characters in the 正 category are formed from 正.

shuowen:1087.text: The Spring and Autumn commentary says: “Reversing 正 makes 乏.”

shuowen:1088.text: Straight or correct. Formed from 日 and 正. All characters in the 是 category are formed from 是.

shuowen:1089.text: Correct. Formed from 是, with 韋 indicating the sound. The Spring and Autumn commentary says: “Commit five wrongs.”

shuowen:1090.text: Lacking this particular thing; “it is this that is few or absent,” although other things remain present. Formed from 是 and 少. This explanation is attributed to Palace Attendant Jia.

shuowen:1091.text: To walk and stop by turns. Formed from 彳 and 止. All characters in the 辵 category are formed from 辵. Read like 辵 in the Gongyang Spring and Autumn commentary's “Leap the steps and run.”

shuowen:1092.text: The place where one steps. Formed from 辵, with 亦 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1093.text: Without disobedience. Formed from 辵, with 𤛉 indicating the sound. Read like 害.

shuowen:1094.text: To guide in front. Formed from 辵, with 率 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1095.text: To travel far. Formed from 辵, with abbreviated 蠆 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1096.text: The appearance of moving along. Formed from 辵, with 川 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1097.text: To walk respectfully and carefully. Formed from 辵, with 㲃 indicating the sound. Read like 九.

shuowen:1098.text: To go on foot. Formed from 辵, with 土 indicating the sound.

shuowen:1099.text: To travel along a path or shortcut. Formed from 辵, with 䌛 indicating the sound. [Duan questions the received wording 行邎徑 and favors 行徑 or 行由徑.]

shuowen:1100.text: To proceed correctly. Formed from 辵, with 正 indicating the sound.
